manuscript.summary: The open manuscript (/Users/pat/code/ACE/paper/aistats_ace_2027/paper.tex, byte-identical to tag archive/delivery-scm-2026-11-02) is a TMLR-format, anonymous paper titled "From Experimental Histories to Causal Surrogates: Data Reuse, Optimization, and Error Propagation". Lines 1-3015 are a generated bundle of 16 embedded companion files (TMLR style, bst, bib, macro files, tables, theory). The narrative runs from line 3022 to 4559. It assesses post-collection refitting ("delivery") of known-graph SCM surrogates on fixed histories. Its confirmatory core is mixed: delivery beats a flat refit in both families and beats rolling at 30 nodes, but is 2.46 times worse than rolling at 5 nodes, undiagnosed. It contains no LLM, DPO, acquisition policy or experimental-cost result. Acquisition appears only in four disclaimers. It has been on submission hold since November 2 as a supporting component study. Reusable for the broader paper: notation, three elementary propositions, the final-refit control arm, the registered-analysis template and negative controls. Every headline element is missing. Internal reviews flag narrow generality, tiny absolute errors, unequal compute, seed sensitivity and the unexplained reversal. No venue or deadline is committed for the broader paper.

implications_for_agenda: Do not propose repeating delivery studies A/B/C or editing the archived manuscript. Use it as a supporting section, a source of theory lemmas, and a predeclared final-refit arm crossed with intervention policies.

Cheap strengthening of the supporting component uses saved artifacts: diagnose the five-node reversal from the 640 checkpoints (teacher-forced versus free-running error, off-support sensitivity), then add ancestral-root and compute-matched flat controls, seeds for every arm and a noisy variant.

Redesign the policy endpoint before any LLM retraining. Ten of 24 systems start at target, first crossing rewards volatile curves, and rankings change under sustained attainment. Pre-register a sustained or area-under-curve endpoint with thresholds calibrated on training systems.

Size the confirmation by power analysis. Paired SD is about 6 cost units, so a 1-unit gain over target risk needs roughly 280 systems. The agenda's 30-50 per family is likely underpowered without variance reduction.

Run a headroom audit first. Target risk leads menu coverage by only 0.83 cost units. Propose regimes where a numerical planner is handicapped: misspecified mechanisms, large or compositional action menus, objectives and costs stated in prose, fallible semantic priors.

Add the absent ablations: SCM-free and graph-removed arms, anonymized and misleading metadata, shuffled feedback, model size, compute-matched ranker. Diagnose state sensitivity for the numerical ranker as well as the LLM arms.
Theory to add: a support-collapse result for constant-action policies built on Prop 8.3, the agenda's kappa + 2 epsilon + delta decomposition, and an exact linear-Gaussian design reference.
Writing debt: rebuild related work, add data figures, re-verify every citation taken from older drafts, and never cite pre-audit LLM numbers or the stale paper.pdf.
No deadline exists, so sequence work by evidence gates. TMLR's claims-and-evidence standard suits a scoped or diagnostic paper if an LLM benefit stays absent.

mechanism.summary: The LLM arms never score commands. Each decision is one Qwen3 chat prompt (fixed instruction, canonical JSON of the whole public envelope, "Decision:"), thinking disabled, then greedy token-by-token generation constrained to a trie of the legal commands. Only four tokens are free: action/stop, observe/set, _x/_y/_xy, _neg/_zero/_pos. I reproduced all 1,698 saved deployment prompts exactly from saved token IDs (every recorded hash matches). Prompts are 1,990 to 4,160 tokens, never truncated. Numbers are 16 to 17 digit floats tokenized one digit per token. The information needed is present but not decision-ready: the frozen planner, given the same prompt content, finds a clearly better action in about 90% of LLM states. No LLM score vectors were saved. Saved training artifacts already point to supervision and optimization, not only the interface: post-SFT likelihoods are 82% command identity, SFT stayed at uniform-guess level out of sample, DPO amplified the SFT prior about 2.5-fold without improving pair agreement, and the matched numerical ranker collapsed too.

key_facts.fact: Action selection is constrained greedy generation, not likelihood scoring: do_sample=False, num_beams=1, prefix_allowed_tokens_fn over a finite grammar. No sum, mean or length normalization exists at deployment. Ties fall to argmax.

I reconstructed the recipe from code, the scientific contract and the executed plan, then checked it against saved training evidence (JSON only, no weights loaded, nothing run). The recipe is 160 single-example SFT updates on mixed-teacher labels, then 119 single-pair DPO updates, one pass each. The saved artifacts show the constant action on the training states themselves: the SFT adapter emits set_x_neg at 108 of 128 nonterminal training states and the final adapter at 123 of 128. SFT never beat a state-blind label-frequency baseline. DPO did not fit its own pairs and lowered the likelihood of both chosen and rejected commands. The exposure-matched numerical ranker stayed near uniform and also deployed only two actions. The evidence points at data and exposure, not specifically at the language model.

key_facts.fact: Data: 32 training worlds, one trajectory each driven by one of four numerical behavior policies (8 worlds each), 5 snapshots at acquisition-cost milestones 0/6/12/18/24, giving 160 SFT records (128 nonterminal, 32 terminal stop). No LLM-visited states. 697 behavior-decision states were saved but only the snapshots were used.

SFT labels come from four teachers rotated by snapshot index, 32 nonterminal labels each, with no teacher identity in the prompt. uniform_random labels are noise by construction. menu_coverage is set_x_neg at snapshot 0 in 8 of 8 worlds (alphabetical tie-break). 17 of 32 target_risk labels are within 2 Monte Carlo SE of the runner-up.

SFT: 160 updates, batch 1, one epoch in fixed roster order, AdamW lr 1e-4 constant (no warmup or decay), betas 0.9/0.999, weight decay 0, clip norm 1.0 (149 of 160 steps clipped). LoRA rank 8, alpha 16, no dropout, q_proj and v_proj of 28 layers, 1,146,880 parameters. Limit 8,192 tokens, no truncation (prompts 1,998-4,199). Loss is mean NLL over command tokens plus EOS only. bf16 base, fp32 adapters and projection, eval mode, seed 109.

Preference data: at each of 128 nonterminal states all 8 actions were branched once per replicate with 4 replicates from the same forked learner. Label is mean replicated NMSE reduction per cost unit. Tie if |mean difference| <= 2 x paired SE (ddof 1, n=4), gap 0. Pairs are within-state only. 3,584 comparisons gave 687 strict and 2,897 ties.

Only 119 pairs were used because the exposure rule takes at most one strict pair per record, the one with the smallest SHA-256 of [domain, record_id, sorted command pair]. Nine nonterminal records had no strict pair. 568 strict pairs were never exposed. Each exposed pair was seen once.

DPO: loss -logsigmoid(beta*[(logp_chosen - ref_chosen) - (logp_rejected - ref_rejected)]), beta 0.1, full-prompt-conditioned command sequence log-likelihoods, reference is the fixed post-SFT adapter, one pair per step, same AdamW object with moments carried over, lr 1e-4, 119 updates all clipped, fixed final checkpoint at step index 278 with no selection.

Numerical ranker: 8,891-wide signed-log state-plus-candidate features, MLP 128-128-1 tanh, 1,154,817 parameters, softmax cross-entropy SFT and categorical DPO (beta 0.1), Adam lr 1e-3. Matched exposure means the identical ordered 160 records and 119 pairs, nothing else. Its nonterminal SFT loss stayed at 2.03-2.15 nats (ln 9 = 2.197) and DPO loss at 0.6934 (ln 2 = 0.6931).

Collapse is visible on the training states. SFT adapter greedy output: set_x_neg 108, observe_all 19, set_x_pos 1 of 128 (agreement with its labels 36/128, modal-label baseline 32/128). Final adapter: set_x_neg 123, set_x_pos 5. Acceptance checked legality and reload only.

SFT prequential NLL per nonterminal example was 3.88, 2.25, 2.57, 2.17 nats by quarter, versus 2.12, 1.92, 1.98, 1.88 for a state-blind online label-frequency counter. The LLM learned format, terminal stop and a coarse history-length effect, with no evidence of posterior-conditional learning.

DPO did not fit: mean loss 0.7395 versus ln 2 = 0.6931, 55 of 118 later steps below ln 2. Final adapter prefers the chosen action on 76 of 119 exposed pairs versus 66 for the reference. Chosen log-likelihood fell 4.69 nats and rejected 6.68 on average. set_x_neg rose 0.57 while set_x_pos fell 3.84.

Preference labels look majority-noise: strict share 19.2 percent versus 13.9 percent expected from a t3 null, 45 percent of mean gains negative, strict pairs agree with the target-risk ordering 123/179, and pair directions across states match coin flips (0.582 versus null 0.580).

Gradient diagnostics established numerical facts only: finite nonzero adapter gradients at every step, exact repeatability under strict determinism, full versus selected projection equality after the fixed-row FP32 fix, changed adapters and unchanged base. They did not test state-conditional signal, held-out loss or action diversity.

implications_for_agenda: Lead with the zero-GPU diagnosis. Saved artifacts already show the constant action at training time, no learning beyond a state-blind baseline, and a DPO stage that failed its own pairs. No new training run is needed to establish this.

Require a behavioral gate in every future training freeze: action histogram, accuracy versus the modal-label baseline, held-out loss versus a state-blind baseline, and held-out pair accuracy versus 50 percent, all before deployment.

Do not scale measured-preference DPO as is. It consumed 9,216 of 10,240 collection cost units for 119 noisy single-pair updates. Prefer listwise soft targets from target-risk scores, or first measure label noise with exact expected gains or 16 replicates.

Repair the supervised target before judging the LLM: one competent teacher or explicit teacher identity, no uniform-random labels, no terminal stop examples, no alphabetical tie-breaks, several shuffled epochs, held-out worlds.

Train the numerical ranker to convergence on CPU as the first learnability probe and as an honest learned control. The current ranker arm is nearly untrained and should not be called a strong control.

Use free data: 697 saved decision envelopes plus zero-response target-risk relabeling give about five times more states with full score vectors. They share the same 32 worlds, so cross-validate by world.
Add an action-renaming experiment (single-token labels, permuted order) to test whether the collapsed action follows the label marginal and tie-break order rather than X = -1 itself.

Engine supports up to 16,384 scheduled steps with repeats, and the whole 279-step run took under five minutes of one 20 GB slice. The exposure planner and scientific worker contract hard-code one pass and need a new reviewed version.

numerics-protocol.summary:
The screen used three-node linear-Gaussian SCMs (chain, fork, collider) with publicly known noise and a conjugate per-mechanism Bayesian linear learner. "Matched" means true edges are drawn from the learner's own N(0,1) prior; "shifted" means edge mean 1.5 under that same prior; low/high is noise variance 0.25/1.0. The 0.04 threshold and 8+24 budget were prospective diagnostic choices with no attainment or power calculation.

Per head, posterior covariance depends only on design rows. But child rows contain random parent responses unless the parent is clamped, and the target is a product of coefficients across heads, so its variance depends on posterior means and the best design is state-dependent. Measured on the 24 saved post-initialization states (working-model expectations, validated by exact replay of saved runs): sequential adaptation after initialization is worth about nothing (−0.7% ± 1.7%); a design planned once from the post-initialization state equals target risk; a good schedule depending only on graph and cost menu is 9 to 21% worse in expected final NMSE.

Target risk is a noisy 32-draw one-step ratio heuristic, not the Bayes rule for the declared endpoint, yet it sits at the state-conditional optimum of this class. The declared endpoint could not resolve any of this: 10 systems tie at the floor (9.9 expected from the learner's own posterior), paired SE is 1.1 to 1.4 cost units, and the expected z for state-adaptive versus good static was 0.75 (about 340 systems needed). The eight-arm ordering is reproduced from the arms' action sequences alone.

key_facts.fact: Regimes are (edge mean, noise variance): matched_low (0, 0.25), matched_high (0, 1), shifted_low (1.5, 0.25), shifted_high (1.5, 1). Intercepts and edges have SD 1. Noise is public and equals truth. One world per regime x graph x cost menu, single keyed Gaussian draws, no selection.

Queries are the eight menu interventions asking for the noise-free mean of Z (weights 1/8, scale 2, tolerance 0.04). They are not distinct: chain q6=q7; fork q0=q4=q5=q6 and q1=q7. X=-1 therefore carries double weight.

key_facts.fact: Learner: independent conjugate linear regressions, known noise, prior N(0, I). The covariance update uses the design row only; a child's row holds the parent's random response unless the parent is clamped.

implications_for_agenda: Do not rerun this world class hoping to show an LLM beating target risk. Target risk is at the state-conditional optimum, sequential gain is about zero, and maximum headroom on the endpoint is 3 cost units against a paired SE near 1.3.

Replace the primary endpoint. Use public posterior-risk curves and noise-free design-quality scoring, add replicate episodes and common exogenous noise across arms. Realized first crossing needs hundreds of systems for effects that posterior risk shows with under 20.

Before any LLM training in a new world class, run a GPU-free headroom audit: tuned public-static schedule, plan-once, myopic target risk, and a rollout or dynamic-programming bound. Proceed only where the gap is detectable at the planned sample size.

Diagnose existing and candidate policies with zero new systems by scoring first decisions and action multisets on the saved states. A state-sensitive policy must switch between x- and x+ and must observe.

Add the controls the screen lacked: a tuned public-only static schedule, plan-once, target risk with a posterior-risk stop rule, and an informed-prior numerical control. This exceeds the current eight-arm limit.

Candidate successor classes in rising code cost: varied text priors with few initial observations and varied query laws (small to medium); wrong or unknown heteroscedastic noise (small to large); nonlinear truth (medium); graph uncertainty (large, the natural home of adaptivity); typed continuous actions (large).

Repair the task law: remove duplicate queries, vary queries per system, use per-system scale (already supported), and set thresholds by preposterior calculation so initial crossing probability is near zero.
For confirmation, lift the development-only scope checks in three modules and the 64-world cap, and add an inferential reporting layer; current reporting is descriptive only.

Heterogeneous costs created no budget structure: target risk used cost-2 actions in 16 of 272 decisions.

prior-evidence-core.summary: No experiment in either repository shows an LLM proposer or policy beating a non-LLM control. The original ACE headline claims were invalidated by a four-confound metric audit: after matching the learner the 5-node result is a tie, and at 15 to 50 nodes ACE with DPO loses to Random. Mission-1 (pre-registered, 11 paired seeds, one emulator) gave an LLM versus random-proposer error ratio of 1.0412, inconclusive. My read-only analysis of its saved bundles shows the "LLM arm" was mostly hand-coded coverage fills plus the prompt's own few-shot example, so that study says the old pipeline's LLM added nothing but says little about what an LLM could add. The delivery (refit) results are solid learner effects, not acquisition evidence, and include an undiagnosed adverse 5-node prospective contrast. The CURC PEV ladder was never run. PEV was instead tested in a later persistent-campaign harness: it beat coverage on two synthetic families, failed its shifted-family primary gate, and never separated from naive variance. PEV has no code lineage to the November target-risk planner but is the same family of idea. LLM collapse onto one action is an eleven-month recurring pattern tied to prompt surface features, previously masked by heuristics. November is its first unscaffolded measurement.

key_facts.fact: Audit outcome (135 re-run cells): end-of-campaign non-root MSE per node at N=15/30/50 is ACE+DPO 0.163/0.257/0.271, ACE without DPO 0.076/0.132/0.238, Random 0.059/0.090/0.118. DPO hurts (p<0.001, p=0.009). Baselines used a weaker student, so the loss only strengthens.

Controls never run: random proposer with ACE's learner, 5-node no-DPO, prompt without the parent hint.

implications_for_agenda: Do not scale, retune or rerun DPO or the old pipeline. Diagnose state sensitivity first, and include prompt-surface permutations (menu order, action identifiers, examples, anonymized names) because prior constants tracked the first node, the few-shot example and possibly menu position.

Every new LLM contrast needs a treatment-fidelity report before outcomes: per-candidate provenance (model output, fallback, fill), raw completion bound to parsed and executed action, and action entropy as a function of state.

Establish headroom before testing any policy. Use task families where the best numerical planner clearly beats random and coverage and where initialization does not already meet the target. Mission-1 and the 10 of 24 pre-solved November systems show how ties arise without it.

Treat numerical SCM planning (target risk, PEV family, risk-pair selector) as both the bar and a defensible positive result. It is the only acquisition signal that has replicated, and CPU-only extensions across topologies and misspecification are cheap.

Consider an LLM role on the prior side (mechanism-form elicitation) with rule-based and anonymized controls. It is the only place an LLM output helped (dev only), and the gain was form, not semantics.
Never cite the 5-node win, pre-audit tables, Runner published win rates, old slide numbers, or the IVR formula. Cite delivery only as a learner effect and keep its adverse 5-node contrast visible.

Keep the accepted statistical design: independent systems as units, frozen protocol, Holm, verdicts that include inferior and non-inferior, sample size from development variance (the Mission-1 LLM contrast had sd log 0.175).
Hold device, learner, evaluator and charged-call accounting identical across arms. Reserve fresh seed namespaces; many are consumed.
Avoid experiments that depend on ace_experiments.py on GPU (unsolved host-RAM leak) or on Runner cloud images (registry deleted).

prior-evidence-portfolio.summary: Since the September 2026 metric audit voided every original ACE-vs-baseline claim, the project has run five successive agendas. Every positive result is numerical or learner-side: delivery refit, SCM surrogate versus flat surrogate (dev), posterior-risk pair selection on two of three synthetic graph families, target-risk planning (best of eight in November), PEV-style model scoring on two of five ACE-Runner scenarios (dev), and cost-aware partial evaluation (dev, hypothetical costs). Every tested LLM role tied or lost to a data-only control: per-step proposing (original ACE, preregistered Mission-1, November DPO), mechanism-family proposals (BoxingGym Lotka, six invalid outputs on 9 October), and partial-identification reasoning. Semantic priors have one small supporting signal that vanished inside a strong learner. Action compilation from independent descriptions was never run with any model and is blocked on a human adjudicator. Translating varied objectives is untested. No external testbed yielded a usable adaptive task: CausalMan's probe menu was rejected, Causal Chambers is logged data that a two-coefficient law explains, NeuronBench rankings depend on the forecaster, and the compressor exists only as slides. ACE-Runner's five simulators are the only ready executable engineering environments. The set-transformer, memory, representation, hypothesis-search and perturbation-data packages were never started.

literature-policy.summary: All ten works cited in the agenda exist and are described accurately. The agenda misses the closest prior art. Trained LLM information-gathering policies now include Paprika (SFT then SFT+DPO, ICML 2025), ASIG, and Kriz et al. (arXiv, Oct 2026), whose mechanism check trains the same base model, Qwen3-0.6B, to a state-dependent selection policy with on-policy GRPO. Numerical amortized intervention policies (CAASL, NeurIPS 2024. GO-CBED, TMLR 09/2026) already cover goal-oriented causal design and claim transfer. The careful ablations (Gupta, Kristiadi, BoxingGym, EVOLvE, Krishnamurthy) agree: LLMs supply priors and proposals, rarely adaptation to measurements, and LLM students distilled from numerical teachers trail them. The constant action has eight documented candidate causes, most separable offline on saved artifacts. The completed screen (known graph, linear, known noise, eight actions, anonymous variables) is the regime where the literature predicts no LLM advantage. What stays open is narrow: a trained SCM-conditioned LLM policy that passes feedback-shuffling controls and beats goal-oriented numerical planners on cost to target where the planner is handicapped for a reason declared in advance. Coverage is about 130 searches and fetches, not a systematic review.

literature-benchmarks.summary:
Read-only web research on 2026-11-12; nothing was installed, run or signed up for.

The main finding is that the local Causal Chambers assessment is outdated. There is now a self-service Remote Lab with a real-time Python API to physical wind and light tunnels, billed per second, and the pip package ships MIT-licensed mechanistic simulators. It is the only candidate I found that combines a validated causal graph, real do-operations, a monetary cost and prose variable descriptions.

Ranked shortlist for the concrete experimentalist task (effort figures are my estimates; no tool was prototyped):
1. Causal Chambers wind tunnel: simulator-backed development (about 1 week), then frozen policies on real hardware (1 to 2 weeks plus human sign-up and budget). Claim scope is one apparatus.
2. Compressor rig: pyCycle (pure Python, 1 to 2 weeks) or ThermoPower via OpenModelica and FMPy (2 to 3 weeks). Simulation only, synthetic costs.
3. BoxingGym location finding, temporal discounting and death process (3 to 5 days each; adapters partly exist). No costs, not do-operations.
4. bnlearn networks with supplied graphs (Gaussian nets 3 to 5 days; discrete nets 1 to 2 weeks). No natural cost, memorization risk.
5. A PhysGym-style prior ladder applied as a control inside options 1 to 4.

Gene-perturbation pools, SERGIO and Tennessee Eastman are poor fits or unverified. CLeaR 2027 closes in four days; ICML 2027 is the next announced deadline.

key_facts.fact: Causal Chambers Remote Lab gives exclusive real-time sessions (set, measure, wait, batches) on physical Wind Tunnel Mk2 and Light Tunnel Mk2 via a sign-up form. One credit is one second of runtime; academic rate 0.014 EUR per credit; 1000 free credits; minimum session 60 s.

The pip package causalchamber (MIT; 0.2.8; pre-release 1.0.0rc1 of 2026-10-29 needs Python 3.11+) includes numpy-only wind-tunnel simulators: ModelA1/A2 (fan speed), ModelB1 (current), SimA1C2/SimA1C3/SimA2C3 (noisy downwind pressure from load_in, load_out, hatch). It is not installed locally.

key_facts.fact: The chamber physics is documented with stated misspecification: affinity-law speed, cubic current, squared-speed pressure, linear hatch term, fans modelled independently although coupled. Graph edges were validated by randomized experiments with KS tests (one wind-tunnel edge p = 0.082).

Remote Lab terms v1.1: bot-registered accounts are not authorised; automated use allowed without unreasonable load; rate limits possible; at least 98% availability; generated data jointly owned and publishable; company may use the customer's name for marketing.

ThermoPower 4.0.0 (Modelica License 2) has IdealGas.Compressor with beta-line map tables. TestCompressorConstSpeed, TestCompressorInertia and both BraytonCycle simulators ran in the OpenModelica master nightly of 2026-11-12 (97 of 100 models simulate). OpenModelica has no official macOS binaries after 1.16; omc and fmpy are absent locally, docker is present.

pyCycle is Apache-2.0 (pip om-pycycle, 4.2.0) and ships compressor map files (axi5, HPC_map, LPC_map, Fan_map, ncp01). TESPy is MIT but its map formulation has no rotational-speed parameter. Neither was run, so suitability for a single compressor rig is unknown.

BoxingGym: MIT, 10 environments, prior versus no-prior variants, 5 runs with standard errors, no tests, no cost model. Priors do not reliably help. Three environments match the Deep Adaptive Design tasks (location finding T=30, temporal discounting T=20, death process T=4).

Whether LLMs use experimental feedback is contested. Gupta et al. 2025: permuted feedback left performance unchanged and classical methods usually won. arXiv 2603.26177: feedback gives +53.4% discoveries (p = 0.003), only for the stronger model. Superiority over the planner is close to unattainable in the linear-Gaussian known-noise family, where a static design is nearly optimal. Either target noninferiority at lower compute, or move to environments where adaptivity or semantic information matters.

verification.overall: The earlier analysis is numerically sound. Every count, mean, SD, p-value and sample size I re-derived from cells.csv and curves.csv matches, and the CSVs match the original 192 reports. I found no arithmetic error. Three statements are worded more strongly than the data allow. First, the "opens with the far X extreme" figures (23/24, 24/24) describe the first pure X-extreme action anywhere in the run. The literal first action gives 17/24 and 22/24. Second, the two shuffle baselines for the fixed-sequence agreement do not reproduce under one definition. Sequences are indeed far from fixed, but target risk is more state dependent than "an action mix plus one sign bit". Third, "power 0.68 for an oracle at the floor" is a normal-theory figure. A policy that dominated target risk system by system would very probably have been detected (exact sign-flip p 0.0039 on the realized floor contrast). What the screen could not detect is a noisy policy with a modestly better mean, because the 3.04-unit ceiling is about the size of the detectable difference. All statistics are descriptive, post hoc and development-data only. On the 14 informative systems local information leads (mean log-area -1.755 vs -1.624, lower on 9 of 14, sign-flip p 0.32). On the 10 at-target systems local information is last of eight (+0.259 vs target risk, p 0.088). Neither is resolved.

Tighter thresholds discriminate more, post hoc. At 0.02 target risk separates from random, coverage, ranker, frozen, supervised and DPO (p 0.0004 to 0.035) but not local information (0.20). At 0.01 all seven are below 0.05, including coverage (+3.875, p 0.0007). Final NMSE and sustained cost separate nothing.

Restricting to the 14 informative systems, the median paired SD is 7.53 and the equivalent of a 1-unit mixed-system difference needs 154 informative systems instead of 305 mixed ones. Excluding at-target systems by design roughly halves the number of systems.

Target risk's action mix varies strongly between systems inside a graph-by-menu cell (chain/uniform observation share 0.25 to 0.71, Y share 0 to 0.58). Cell membership adds nothing to step prediction (label-shuffle p 0.11). Step position adds a little (order-shuffle p 0.003). A constant 'always observe' guess matches local information as well as a per-cell fixed sequence (0.558 vs 0.570).

The near-side split is not specific to DPO. The frozen LLM, which never intervenes, shows a similar deficit on the same 7 systems (+0.426 vs +0.096, p 0.055), and DPO minus frozen does not split (p 0.32). The pattern separates arms that never set X at the far extreme from arms that do. It is post hoc on 7 systems.

findings.summary:
The constant action is already in the saved training evidence, so it is not a training-to-development shift. On the 128 nonterminal training prompts the supervised checkpoint generates set_x_neg 108 times and the DPO checkpoint 123 times. They match the teacher label in 36 and 32 cases, against 32 for a constant.

Supervised labels are only mildly imbalanced (set_x_neg is 25% of nonterminal targets), but set_x_neg is the plurality at every token decision of the command, and greedy trie decoding follows that path. additional_findings: The in-sample 56.8% of a constant ranking is what noise alone gives. Relabelling the 8 actions at random within each record yields 56.5% on average (p 0.45). The coin-flip null (54.1%) ignores within-record dependence. There is no detectable state-independent preference signal.

The label signal that exists is state-specific. Strict labels agree with the state's own target-risk ordering in 68.7% of pairs, but in 50.2% when paired with another state's planner scores (p 0.0005) and 51.4% with the average planner ordering. Local information: 67.0% against 51.6% (p 0.0055). This is the positive evidence verdict iii lacked.

Neither checkpoint tracks labels on its own training states. Final table: teacher label scores -0.16 nats relative to that command's same-snapshot mean (p 0.86). SFT: +0.09 nats (n 27, p 0.18). Within-state, label log-likelihood is -2.168 before the model's own SFT update and -2.177 at the end of the pass (n 14).

The supervised neglect of set_x_pos appeared late. Geometric-mean probability on set_x_pos labels was 0.341 in steps 80-119 and 0.173 in steps 120-159. In the same states it fell from 0.195 to 0.084 by the end of the pass (n 6). The last 30 steps hold 8 set_x_neg labels and 2 set_x_pos. Recency weighting gives at most 1.6 to 1, so it is not sufficient. Pass order is an untested contributor that needs a reshuffled rerun.

Token-greedy decoding is not command argmax. At the SFT checkpoint, snapshots 1-3, saved geometric-mean probabilities are observe_all 0.367 and set_x_neg 0.345, yet greedy output is set_x_neg in 76 of 96 states. In 11 saved states with P(observe_all) between 0.33 and 0.44 the output is set_x_neg every time. This is an inference from averages.

One toy counterfactual in the earlier notes did not reproduce. With all 687 strict pairs in random order my re-implementation ends at set_x_pos about 65% of the time, not set_x_neg in 478/500. Which command a state-blind learner collapses to is not robust.

DPO barely fit its own pairs: loss 0.6811 against 0.6931 at the reference, 45/119 moved against their label. It amplified the SFT ordering instead (slope 3.45 of final on SFT score differences, r 0.79).

Between 69% and 73% of the 687 strict labels are what the tie rule passes under no difference. Mean NMSE reduction from one extra response falls from 0.0230 at snapshot 0 to 0.0013 at snapshot 3, where only 50.0% of mean gains are positive.
Where a teacher's label appears in a strict pair it is preferred 45 times and rejected 11 for local information, against 35/19 for target risk, 30/26 for menu coverage and 16/13 for uniform random.

The summary sentence that the behavior is not a training-to-development shift holds for the constant action only. SFT never generates stop on nonterminal training prompts (0/128), and stop labels exist only at zero budget. The supervised arm's early stopping in deployment therefore sits in budget states training never covered (inference, deployment data not opened). Training histories also come only from the four numerical behavior policies.

open_questions: Do frozen, SFT and DPO score vectors vary with the state below the argmax, and how large are the command gaps? Only a scoring pass can answer.
Why does the SFT adapter give x+ about 0.05 probability on training states when x+ is 29 of 160 labels, against 0.41 for x- with 32?

surprises_or_contradictions: The brief's file counts are low: 35,582 files under launch/cpu and 11,564 under launch/gpu, not about 7,100 and 2,100. The LLM arms' episode directories are not in the local copies at all.
The supervised adapter is not state-blind. It keys on budget level, graph and remaining budget, and those patterns mirror training snapshot levels and label statistics rather than the planner.
The exposed DPO pairs did not favour x- (chosen 14, rejected 9 of 119; x+ had the largest net count). The ranker trained on the same exposure went to x+, the LLM to x-.
DPO and SFT beat uniform random over the first four decisions; the damage comes from never switching.
The reference planner's own choices are mostly Monte Carlo ties after the first three decisions, so its argmax is a poor label and a poor agreement target.
Arms that pick the same first action still see different states from decision 1, so only decision 0 is a matched comparison.

verification.overall: No claim was refuted. Every headline number reproduces from the raw records with my own code: the decision table, the absence of LLM scores, first-decision agreement, x- as TR optimum in 11/24, the regret table, and the SFT, frozen, ranker, token and training counts. Four items are partial: the 256-draw 'identical' statement (seed luck from exact ties), the risk/NMSE ratio (1.008, not 0.994), the drift R2 (0.60-0.75, not 0.84), and the reading that SFT is 'state-dependent' (it is budget-keyed, with no sign of posterior use). The interpretations need tightening before they drive the agenda: the headline endpoint cannot separate SFT from DPO, the regret proxy is not validated against outcomes, and the logged DPO drift does not explain why only x- is emitted. Full notes: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-pat--claude-spares-spare-Yk5OYw/579351c9-7517-4194-a931-08cc9167484d/scratchpad/w1/deployment-forensics-verify.md. Per-decision table with reference scores: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-pat--claude-spares-spare-Yk5OYw/579351c9-7517-4194-a931-08cc9167484d/scratchpad/w1/deployment-forensics-verify/decisions_verifier.csv.
additional_findings: Endpoint noise floor: SFT and DPO issue identical actions for their first 10-22 acquisitions in every world but have separate measurement streams. Their capped cost differs in 11/24 worlds, and in 8 of those the difference was decided inside the identical prefix (for example world 21: 32 vs 12; world 16: 10 vs 22). Those noise-only differences total 54 cost units against a reported mean difference of 0.54. Ten worlds already meet the target at initialization, so 14 carry endpoint information.

Missing LLM scores are recoverable without new environment responses: local sft.adapter.pt and final.adapter.pt hash to the deployed adapter pins (583b1659..., 6f540dfe...), and all 1,698 exact prompt token sequences are saved. A Qwen3-0.6B snapshot is in the local cache, pin not verified. I did not run it.

DPO-stage logs do not explain 'x- only': shifts favour observe in 19/19 exposed pairs containing it (mean +6.7 nats, although observe was the rejected command in 13) and x- in 20/23 (+3.3). The single direct observe-vs-x- pair moved 1.37 nats toward observe. Deployed DPO emitted observe 0/576 times. Token-tree pooling, off-distribution states or later updates could explain this; the records cannot separate them.
Stop appears in 0 of 3,584 preference pairs, yet DPO removed every stop (SFT stopped in 23/24 worlds, DPO in 0/24). The DPO stage changed behaviour that no label addressed.

Position, identity and tie rule are confounded: menu order is identical in all 4,371 deployment states and 160 training records, and the task payload is byte-identical everywhere. Frozen emits the first menu entry; SFT and DPO emit the first listed intervention, which also wins every alphabetical tie rule. Protocol source (llm_intervention_screen_protocol.py:126-132,188) assigns a quarter of labels each to random, menu-coverage, local-information and target-risk teachers; read in source, not recomputed per record.

Off-distribution deployment states: the longest run of one repeated acquisition in any training history is 10 (129/160 have runs of 3 or less). DPO states from decision 11 onward (312/576) contain 11-23 consecutive x- rows.

The ranker is not equally state-blind early: at decision 0 it deviates to x+ in three worlds and is right in all three; relative regret in decisions 0-3 is 0.219 against 0.337 (DPO) and 0.340 (SFT). It then switches to x+ on a step-indexed schedule (never x- after decision 11) while the reference prefers x- in 260/288 of those states.

On regret DPO is indistinguishable from frozen (worse in 12/24 worlds, p 0.79) and worse than SFT in 19-22/24 (p <= 0.001). An all-observe policy has regret 0.654 yet the fourth-best final NMSE, so the one-step proxy should be validated before it becomes a primary endpoint.
